findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past/missing the correct date marking. Discussed with PIC, items that were missing dates were properly date marked, and items held past date marking maximum were discarded. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked, and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed washing hands and turning off the faucet without using a barrier. CORRECTED - The employee was educated by the inspector on proper handwashing procedures, and the person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to review proper handwashing practices with all employees. Ensure a barrier, such as a paper towel, is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Cleaned cooking utensils stored on the dish rack were observed to have food debris remaining on the surfaces. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the utensils were returned to the dish machine for re-washing. Ensure all cooking utensils are properly washed and maintained free of food debris before being stored for use.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Chicken in batter (a time/temperature control for safety [TCS] food) was observed in the walk-in cooler with date marking exceeding the maximum allowable holding time of 7 days. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the product was voluntarily discarded. Ensure date marks on TCS foods are routinely monitored and all TCS foods are discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

findings.comment:

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

1) An accumulation of food debris present on the top and sides of dish machine. 
2) An accumulation of grease and food debris present in between grills. 
3) An accumulation of food debris inside 4 microwaves throughout kitchen, mainly the inside roofs of microwaves.

Discussed with PIC, ensure all non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents grease and food debris accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed sani buckets to be low - 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Ensure sani buckets are changed frequently to maintain concentration of 200-400 ppm. Facility has test strips to verify concentration levels. Ensure staff is aware to change the buckets every 4 hours or so to maintain the concentration. Discussed with PIC. Buckets all re-made - 400 ppm. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/16/23.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

(REPEAT) Observed the shelving of the walk-in freezer to have a large amount of food and waste debris. Ensure staff is aware to frequently sweep out under the shelving units. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 9/20/22 and 2/16/23. Discussed with PIC. Correct behavior by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas of the facility in need of caulking and/or re-caulking:
1. Hand sink near the ice machine has moldy caulk - re-caulk the sink to the wall.
2. Hot holding steam table along the cook line has moldy caulk - re-caulk the steam table to the cook line wall.
3. Multiple areas with tiny holes in the wall (fill with caulking): above the mixer/meat slicer area, by the hand sink wall across from the dish machine area, along the cook line wall (hot holding/cold holding side, not the grill side). 
4. Hand sink at front server area (across from the cashier area) has missing and coming away caulking in the interior creases of the sink - re-caulk.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure the caulking is re-done before the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/26/23.

The wall in the chemical storage room has dry wall dis repaired. Ensure repairs to the wall so it is smooth and easily cleanable. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed a company vomit/diarrhea policy and SCDPH’s policy; however, the facility has no way to perform the procedure. There is no bleach or a biohazard kit that kills for Norovirus. Discussed situation with PIC. Ensure to purchase a biohazard kit that specifically kills for Norovirus and/or buy bleach to be able to perform the procedure outlined in the policy. Inspector will follow-up on 2/27/23.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed improper hand washing: no barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles after properly washing hands. Discussed with employee who improperly washed hands and requested to re-wash hands correctly. Ensure staff is aware of proper hand washing technique in order to prevent cross contamination of hands: soap, hot water, lather for 20 seconds, wash hands, dry with paper towels, turn off faucets with a barrier such as the paper towel in order to not re-contaminate hands. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed improper storage order within the walk-in cooler: chicken was above ground beef. Inspector moved the chicken to the bottom of the cooler shelf. Ensure staff is aware of proper storage order. Chicken should always be on the bottom shelf. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational handout regarding storage order. Post on walk-in cooler door. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

(B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed both sani buckets to be low in concentration - 100 ppm. Facility is utilizing quaternary ammonium for sanitizer. Concentrations should be 200-400 ppm. Discussed with PIC. Ensure sani buckets are frequently changed in order to maintain appropriate concentrations. Facility has test strips to verify. COS.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:

Observed the following areas no longer smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent:
1. Caulk is needed in various areas (no caulk or moldy caulk that needs replaced): hand sink near ice machine (moldy), hot holding steam table to the wall (moldy), holes in wall by the mixer and slicer, holes in the wall by the hand sink across from dish machine area, hand sink at front server area (across from cashier area - missing caulk in corner).

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure all equipment is flush with the wall by caulking and/or remove old, moldy caulk and repair. Fill holes in walls with caulk. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no copies of food handler’s licenses at the facility. Inspector checked list of approved food handler’s courses on cell phone. Bob Evan’s was not listed. PIC indicated that new employees are supposed to provide proof of food handler’s license and/or CFPM license when onboarding. Ensure all new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Keep copies in a public health binder at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Create a binder/folder by next routine inspection. Food handler’s license are valid for 3 years.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certification for the facility certified food protection manager’s (CFPM’s). All CFPM’s should have additional allergen training certification. Certification is good for 3 years. Provided educational handout regarding where to take training online. Ensure all CFPM’s complete by next routine inspection. Keep copies in the facility public health binder/folder. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Several Risk factor violations have been noted on this inspection. Violations pertaining to line items 21, 22 and 48 will be followed up on October 4th to ensure that the relevant health concerns are being adequately managed moving foreword.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of the inspection, a CFPM certificate was not able to be provided for any employee at the facility. PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The probe apparatus in both of the Alto-Shaam units are observed soiled with dried on food debris. PIC was consulted and the items cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

A container of green beans (with ham) is observed on the prep line steam table with an internal temperature of 110F-114F. Hot holding requires 135F or higher. A conversation with the PIC and an employee indicates that the foods were brought out at approximately 11 am. The container was discarded at 3 pm. It appears that this section of the steam table has been turned down. PIC turned the knob back up to a higher setting to ensure safe temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Containers of tomatoes (both sliced and diced) as well as butter on the prep line are observed with internal temperatures between 54F-58F. TCS foods should be maintained at 41 or less. Foods were discarded by the PIC during the inspection to correct the violation. Education took place and lids were suggested to maintain the temperatures at safe levels throughout the day.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) Knives and spatulas are stored in a container that has a rusty scraper as well as old sanitizer test strips that are discolored. The bottom of the container is also observed soiled. 2) steak knives in the server area are observed with food debris in the bottom of their container (in contact with the eating surfaces). PIC was consulted on both of these locations and the items moved to dish in both cases. PIC instructed to ensure that the food contact surfaces of utensils are stored in locations and ways that protect their eating surfaces until use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-603.14: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be effectively washed to remove or completely loosen soils. (B) Washing procedures selected shall be based on type and purpose of EQUIPMENT and type of soil to be removed. 

Multiple cleaned and sanitized buckets are observed with dried on batter while being stored on the clean side of the dish machine. PIC instructed to ensure that dishes are completely cleaned in their washing cycle. The items were moved back to the dirty side of the process to be cleaned again.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures sanitizer solutions shall be provided. 

A method to verify that dishes are reaching critical temperature in the dish machine is not available at the facility during this inspection. Inspector discussed both maximum registering thermometers and thermo-strips with the PIC and instructed them to ensure that something is available. Inspector will follow up on October 4th for compliance.

1) The batter mixer in the rear of the facility is observed heavily soiled; 2) shelves and fan covers in the reach in cooler to the left of the cook line are in need of cleaning; 3) the reach in cooler and freezer to the right of the cook line is in need of cleaning. PIC is instructed to clean these items and maintain the non-food contact surfaces in the facility clean.

Multiple floor locations throughout the facility are in need of significant cleaning: 1) under the shelves in the walk in cooler; 2) under the shelves in the walk in freezer; 3) behind the cook line; 4) under shelves in the dry storage area. findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the soda fountain machine are observed with bacterial build up. The items were discussed with the PIC and a server and the nozzles removed for cleaning. New nozzles were placed on the machine during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Two trays of bacon are observed on a shelf at room temperature. The trays have date stamps indicating they were prepared yesterday at 9:10 am and that the items are par cooked. A discussion took place with the PIC to understand the procedure in place for these items. The bacon is par cooked from raw, cooled in the walk in to 40 degrees and then allowed to be out at room temperature. This is a poor practice. Bacon is considered a TCS food until it is thoroughly cooked (which reduces the water activity to safe levels). The trays were discarded during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC is now aware that until bacon is fully cooked it must remain in temperature control, or have a time control policy in place and followed.

findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The three sani buckets in the facility are observed with 0 ppm Quat on the inspector’s test strips. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

On the prep line, the pan of raw eggs is observed over filled so that several eggs are not effectively being cold held. Eggs are observed at 38 in the lower section of the pan and at 50F-62F above the pan. PIC (after consulting employee on the line) stated that the eggs had been pulled from the cooler an hour ago. The eggs out of temperature are being placed back into the cooler to correct and PIC is instructed to ensure that TCS foods are stored in effective cold holding.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Multiple tubs used for storage of cleaned dishes/ utensils are observed soiled. PIC instructed to clean the tubs regularly to maintain the dishes they store in a clean state prior to use.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

The dough mixer in the back of the facility is observed with duck tape used to hold pieces together. The machine as well as the tape is observed with dough splash from today on it. Tape is not considered a cleanable surface as should not be used in areas subject to moisture of food debris/ splash. PIC is instructed to repair/ replace the equipment so that it can be effectively cleaned.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Flies observed in the dish area (5-6). Last pest control visit was on 6/28. PCO comes on a monthly basis. See that PCO visits facility and addresses flies in the dish area. PIC contacted PCO and scheduled a routine visit. 
Fly strips are acceptable to use as long as they do not pose a contamination risk to equipment and utensils. Recommend placing low under dish machine manifold or off to the side where not directly over clean dishes in dish area.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Two cans in the dry storage area are observed with sever dents along the upper seam, lower seam and the side. Education took place explaining the reason for the related safety concerns and the cans were discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple utensil being stored on the hanging rack in the back of the facility are observed with food debris still on the food contact surfaces of the utensils. These utensils are also in contact with other cleaned/ sanitized utensils. PIC was consulted and the entire rack was moved to the dish area. 

2) The surface of the nozzles of the fountain drink machine is observed with an accumulated dark substance believed to be from improper cleaning. The nozzles were moved to cleaning to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Scoops for cinnamon used as a topping were observed with the handles in contact with the foods in the grill area. PIC was consulted to verify that the item was used as a topping and not as part of a recipe. PIC was instructed to ensure that the handles remain out of contact with the foods in order to prevent potential cross contamination. Scoops were moved during the inspection to correct.
